# PRC: an encoder must use the float-precision `origin_array`, not the value it was derived from

**Section:** §7.8.9.7 "Mesh Attribute Structure", Table 175 `origin_array` row
(`iso-prc/definitions/base-entities/tessellation.yaml:512`); the ΔV0 computation in §7.8.9.3
(`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc:2568`).

**Change type:** Normative addition — a conformance requirement on encoders.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(2 September 2026). No such requirement is present.

---

## The asymmetry

`origin_array` is stored at **single precision**:

```yaml
  - name: origin_array
    data_type:
      kind: Array
      inner_kind: FloatAsBytes
      occurrence: "3"
```

and the prose describes it as "three floating point coordinates that describe the bounding box
centre of the compressed 3D tessellation data" (`07-base-entities.adoc:2794`).

But it is *used* in arithmetic that determines every stored coordinate. §7.8.9.3 says:

> "For V0, ΔV0 ← V0 - origin_array is computed and resulting coordinates X,Y,Z are divided by the
> tolerance and rounded to the nearest integer."

A decoder can only ever recover the single-precision value that was written. An encoder that computes
that subtraction against a **higher-precision** origin — a double-precision bounding-box centre it
derived the float from — produces deltas that no decoder can reproduce. Every quantised coordinate is
then off by the truncation residual, and the error does not cancel: it re-enters at every traversal
chain restart, so it compounds with mesh size and topological fragmentation.

Nothing in the current text says the encoder must round-trip the value first.

**This is the only field in the structure with that exposure.** `tolerance`, the other quantity in
the same arithmetic, is declared `Double` and so is stored at full precision — encoder and decoder
necessarily agree on it. `origin_array` is the sole place where the encoder can hold a value the
decoder cannot obtain. That makes the requirement narrow and easy to state.

## Evidence

Root-caused by diffing raw `Δv[]`, origin and basis-vector state between encoder and decoder — not
inferred from symptoms. Reproduced and eliminated identically **across three orders of magnitude of
scale**, at roughly 272, 1,000,000 and 20,000,000 triangles, and confirmed against **two independent
readers** (Adobe Acrobat and PDF-XChange).

The failure presented as progressive geometric corruption that worsened with mesh size — the
signature of an error that re-enters per chain restart rather than a constant offset.

## CR-17a — proposed NOTE

Insert after the `origin_array` row's existing description in Table 175:

> **NOTE — Encoder-side precision consistency.** An encoder's own internal use of `origin_array`,
> including the ΔV0 computation of 7.8.9.3 and any other reference-frame computation depending on
> this value, shall use the same single-precision value that is written by `FloatAsBytes`, not a
> higher-precision value from which it was derived — for example a double-precision bounding-box
> centre. A decoder can recover only the single-precision value from the file. An encoder whose
> internal arithmetic uses a more precise value produces coordinates no conforming decoder can
> reconstruct, and the resulting error compounds with each traversal restart in a large or
> topologically fragmented mesh.

**Placement alternative worth considering.** The row in Table 175 is where `origin_array` is defined,
which is why the NOTE is proposed there. But the hazard arises where the value is *used*, in the ΔV0
sentence at `07-base-entities.adoc:2568`. If the working group would rather the warning sit next to
the arithmetic it governs, that location is arguably more effective; we have no preference beyond it
appearing in one of the two.

## Scope of the claim

The requirement is stated for `origin_array` only, because that is the only field in this structure
where the exposure exists — we checked the others. The general principle (an encoder must not compute
against precision a decoder cannot recover) may apply elsewhere in the document, but we have not
surveyed for it and are not asking for a general clause.

The one other `FloatAsBytes` array in the same file, `texture_parameters`
(`tessellation.yaml:718`), is not used in reconstruction arithmetic and is not affected.
title: PRC: Add `origin_array` Encoder-side Float before Reconstruction

# PRC: Clarify `normal_was_reversed` timing and bulk-array semantics, and remove the `normal_is_reversed` contradiction

**Sections:** base specification §7.8.9.7 prose and Table 175 (`normal_is_reversed` row); companion
*Pseudo-code Additions*, Functions 6 (`CheckIfNormalIsReversed`), 7 (`EvaluateAdjacentTri`) and 12
(`PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` Triangle-Fan Decompression).

**Change type:** Normative correction (Class C) plus pseudocode clarification (Classes A and B).

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(2 September 2026) — not only the published PDF. File and line references below are into that
repository, so they can be acted on directly.

---

## Summary of what is asked for

| Sub-CR | Location | Change | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CR-15d** | §7.8.9.7 prose | **Delete** "The `normal_is_reversed` field is reserved for future use." | **Highest** — direct self-contradiction |
| **CR-15e** | Table 175, `normal_is_reversed` row | State the cardinality as `T` explicitly; replace the borrowed normals-count description | **High** |
| CR-15c | *Pseudo-code Additions*, Function 6 | Replace the per-triangle stream read in the `MustRecalculateNormals == TRUE` branch with a bulk-array lookup; add a NOTE on the `T`-element pre-read | Medium |
| CR-15a | *Pseudo-code Additions*, Function 12 | Insert the one-iteration-lag clarification between `EvaluateAdjacentTri()` and `Normal_Restoration()` | Medium |
| CR-15b | *Pseudo-code Additions*, note before Function 12 | Reconcile the "Normative interleaved decode" note with Function 7's actual input list | Low |

CR-15d and CR-15e are in the base specification and are the two that change what a conforming reader
does. CR-15a–c are pseudocode consistency and can be taken separately.

---

## Class C — the base specification contradicts itself (CR-15d, CR-15e)

Two adjacent sentences in §7.8.9.7 read:

> `-- The number_implicit_normal field is reserved for future use.`
> `-- The normal_is_reversed field is reserved for future use.`

while Table 175 gives the same field a type and an optionality condition:

> `normal_is_reversed    Array <Boolean>[]    (Optional; if must_recalculate_normals is TRUE))`

A reader implementing the prose ignores a field that determines rendering. Both statements are still
present in the working source as of `ba2bdc1` — `07-base-entities.adoc:2816` and `:2818` — so this is
not an artefact of an out-of-date published PDF.

### The field is load-bearing, and we can quantify it

In the `must_recalculate_normals == TRUE` branch this array is the only carrier of per-triangle
orientation; there are no stored normals to compare against. When our encoder left it at its
all-zero default, the aggregate wrong-orientation rate — measured against true source geometry, not
against self-consistency — was **42.4%** across six real files (~1.02 million triangles). Writing it
from geometry brought that to **1.9%**, and flipped two of four test files from an empty model tree
to correct display in Adobe Acrobat.

A field whose value changes a render from blank to correct is not reserved.

### Table 175's cardinality is also unstated

This is easy to miss, because the row looks complete. The bracket is empty — `Array <Boolean>[]` —
and the description attached to it is:

> "The number of normals is implicit, depending on the number of triangles and faces. Vertices have
> always as many normals as the number of faces to which they belong."

That describes **the number of normals**, which is a different quantity from the length of this
boolean array: one is a per-vertex-per-face count, the other is one flag per triangle. The row
currently pairs a boolean array with the cardinality rule for something else.

### CR-15d — proposed edit

In **`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc`**:

**DELETE line 2818:**

```
* The *normal_is_reversed* field is reserved for future use.
```

**And review line 2816** in the same list:

```
* The *number_implicit_normal* field is reserved for future use.
```

Per the resolution proposed on
[#750](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/750), `number_implicit_normal` is a
computed helper rather than a stored field. If it is retained in the prose it should say that,
rather than "reserved for future use".

### CR-15e — proposed edit, and one prerequisite

The row is generated from **`iso-prc/definitions/base-entities/tessellation.yaml`**, where the
`normal_is_reversed` entry currently reads:

```yaml
  - name: normal_is_reversed
    data_type:
      kind: Array
      inner_kind: Boolean
      occurrence:
    required: false
    description: The number of normals is implicit, depending on the number of triangles and faces. Vertices have always as many normals as the number of faces to which they belong.
    require_conditions: "if *must_recalculate_normals* is TRUE)"
```

Three things are visible here that are not visible in the rendered table:

1. **`occurrence:` is empty.** That is why the type renders as `Array <Boolean>[]`. Every other
   array in this file supplies one — e.g. `points_is_reference_array` has
   `occurrence: reference_array_size`.
2. **The stray parenthesis is in the data**, at the end of `require_conditions`, which is what
   produces `TRUE))` in the output. One-character fix.
3. **The `description` is the normals-count text**, which as noted above describes a different
   quantity.

**The prerequisite.** We would ask for `occurrence: T` — but *the document has no name for the
triangle count*. Grepping the source, `triangle_face_array_size` and `number_of_triangles` do not
occur anywhere; the quantity that fixes the length of `edge_status_array`, `triangle_face_array` and
`normal_is_reversed` is never named. By contrast `face_number` **is** defined, at
`07-base-entities.adoc:2832`:

> `* The *face_number* field contains the number of faces in the triangle_face_array and is the maximum index value in triangle_face_array + 1.`

So the cleanest fix is a parallel sentence introducing the triangle count, after which the
cardinality can be stated in the document's own vocabulary. Suggested, in the same list:

> `* The number of triangles is the number of elements in *triangle_face_array*.`

`triangle_face_array` is a `CompressedIndiceArray` and therefore self-describing in length, so this
defines the quantity without adding a stored field.

**Then** the YAML becomes:

```yaml
  - name: normal_is_reversed
    data_type:
      kind: Array
      inner_kind: Boolean
      occurrence: number_of_triangles     # or whatever name the committee prefers
    required: false
    description: "One Boolean per triangle. A TRUE entry indicates that the triangle's reconstructed normal is reversed with respect to its winding. The array is read in bulk before mesh traversal begins, in the same manner as *edge_status_array*; it is not interleaved with the per-triangle decode."
    require_conditions: "if *must_recalculate_normals* is TRUE"
```

**This prerequisite also blocks [#775](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/775)**,
which asks for `reference_array_size = T + 2·S`. That formula cannot be written in the document's
vocabulary either, for the same reason. Naming the triangle count once unblocks both.

It is worth adding that the unnamed quantity is not a bookkeeping abstraction — it is load-bearing,
and measurable. Sampling 60 compressed-tessellation entities from a corpus of real files gathered
from the wild, and taking the difference `reference_array_size − T`:

| | |
|---|---|
| entities sampled | 60 |
| difference always **even** | yes — 0 exceptions |
| difference always **positive** | yes — 0 exceptions |
| difference exactly `+2` (a single shell) | 23 of 60 (38%) |
| implied shell count `S = difference / 2` | 1 to 7,211 |
| largest entity sampled | 1,126,444 triangles |

Under `reference_array_size = T + 2·S` the difference is `2S`, so it must be even and at least 2 —
which is precisely what real files show, with no exception in the sample. So `T` is a quantity two
separate array lengths already depend on, and one that a reader must compute to parse the entity at
all. The document uses it three times over and names it never.

### Relationship to #750

[#750](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/750) asks the same field's length and has
been recommended for closing on the grounds that the answer is already in the current CD table. **The
table half is there; the prose half is not.** We have no objection to #750 closing — we ask only that
CR-15d goes in with it, since closing on the table alone leaves the document asserting both that the
field is an `Array<Boolean>` and that it is reserved.

---

## Class A — one-iteration lag between `EvaluateAdjacentTri` and `Normal_Restoration` (CR-15a)

Function 12's `Repeat` loop calls `EvaluateAdjacentTri()` and then `Normal_Restoration()` on what
reads as the same triangle in one pass. That ordering cannot be executed as written:
`EvaluateAdjacentTri` consumes `normal_was_reversed`, which is produced only by that same triangle's
`Normal_Restoration`.

The resolution is that `EvaluateAdjacentTri` operates on the **previously committed** triangle
(index `i-1`), using the value resolved in the prior pass. The pseudocode is correct in effect but
misleading in presentation, and an implementer following it literally either deadlocks on the
dependency or silently uses an uninitialised value.

**CR-15a:** insert a comment in Function 12's loop body making the lag explicit — that
`EvaluateAdjacentTri()` evaluates the previously committed triangle's forward edges and left/right
assignment, using its already-resolved `normal_was_reversed`, and that the current triangle's own
value is not yet available at that point.

## Class B — bulk array versus interleaved stream reads (CR-15b, CR-15c)

Function 6's `MustRecalculateNormals == TRUE` branch is written as
`ReadBitFromStream(normal_bit_stream)`, i.e. a per-triangle read interleaved with the decode. The
array is in fact read in bulk before traversal, exactly as `edge_status_array` is — the same
correction already applied for that field under CR-14.

**CR-15c:** replace the stream read in Function 6's TRUE branch with a lookup into the pre-read
array, and add a NOTE recording that `normal_is_reversed` is a `T`-element array read before
traversal begins.

**CR-15b:** the note preceding Function 12 describes a "Normative interleaved decode" that is not
consistent with Function 7's input list. Reconcile the two, and relocate the stream-desync hazard
warning to `Normal_Restoration` / `CheckIfNormalIsReversed`, where the hazard actually arises.

---

## Evidence class

CR-15d and CR-15e are direct textual contradictions in the base specification, readable without any
implementation. The quantitative claim above (42.4% → 1.9%, and the two blank-tree files) is from our
own encoder measured against source geometry and confirmed in Adobe Acrobat.

CR-15a–c are read from a reference decoder's source rather than inferred from behaviour, and have not
been cross-checked against independently produced files. They are offered on that basis; if the
committee would rather take only the base-specification items, CR-15d and CR-15e stand alone.

Per-file measurements are available if useful.
title: PRC: Clarify `normal_was_reversed` Timing and Bulk-Array Semantics

## CR-18 — Restore the Missing Orientation-Consistency Step in the Apex Reconstruction Formula (§7.8.9.3 "Mesh Points and Triangles", Formulas (1)-(3))
[New 21 July 2026] related to issue #727

**Sections:** §7.8.9.3 "Mesh Points and Triangles" (ISO/CD 14739-1.4:2026(en), p.79-80), the prose
immediately following Formulas (1)-(3) that reconstructs a new apex vertex `V2` in the local frame of its
entering edge.

**Change type:** Normative correction. The base specification already states a coordinate-frame formula
for this purpose (Formulas (1)-(3)) — this CR does not propose new content so much as **restore a step
the existing formula is missing**, without which the formula does not reliably reconstruct the encoder's
actual output.

**Status:** Confirmed against the nanoPRC reference implementation (CascadiaVoxel LLC, AGPLv3,
https://github.com/mvrhel/nanoPRC) and independently corroborated by ablation testing across five real
files (four small curated meshes plus a 973-part, 397,645-triangle real-world assembly): disabling the
missing step causes hard decode failure on 3 of 4 curated files, gross manifold corruption (thousands of
non-manifold/boundary edges, Euler characteristic off by orders of magnitude) on the 4th, and a whole-file
open failure on the 973-part assembly.

---

### Background

§7.8.9.3 "Mesh Points and Triangles" (p.79-80) already gives a coordinate-frame construction for
reconstructing a new (non-reference) apex vertex `V2` of a triangle entered through edge `[V0 V1]`, with
`V3` the far vertex of the already-treated neighbouring triangle `Tn` across that edge:

> Origin `O ← (V1 + V0) * 0.5`. Other axes are defined in Formulas (1) to (3):
>
> (1) `X ← (V1 - V0) / norm(V1 - V0)`
>
> (2) `Z_temp ← V3 - O` and `Z ← Z_temp × X`
>
> (3) `Y ← Z × X`
>
> In Formula (1), V0 and V1 are taken so that V0 has a treatment index less than V1... A particular case
> occurs if the Z axis or Y are NULL (length less than FLT_EPSILON)... they are computed by the function
> `MakeOrthoRep()`, using the unit axis X as input. Then V2 is expressed in this coordinate system,
> compressed the same way as before and updated in the working structure.

This formula, exactly as written, is **not sufficient to reconstruct a conforming encoder's actual
output** — it omits an orientation-consistency step that determines the sign of `Y` and `Z`, and without
it, a decoder following Formulas (1)-(3) literally reconstructs the correct axis directions only by
chance, roughly half the time.

### Finding

The companion *Pseudo-code Additions* document already documents the missing step, in its own
`ApexFromEdge` function (function 11), which otherwise reproduces Formulas (1)-(3) exactly (same origin,
same `X`, same `Z_temp`/`Z` construction, same `Y`, same treatment-index ordering convention, same
`MakeOrthoRep()` degenerate-axis fallback) — but adds, after Formula (3):

```text
# Orientation test: ensure Y and Z point away from the committed surface
Let w = O - Vfar
If DotProduct(Y, w) > 0.0 Then
    Negate Y
    Negate Z
EndIf
```

Independent testing against nanoPRC's reference decoder (which implements this same orientation test,
expressed as a runtime conditional rather than inlined algebra) confirms this step is not an optional
refinement: it fires on **100% of grown triangles** across all four curated test files (15,077 of 15,077),
meaning it is not "conditional" in practice at all on real encoder output — every single reconstructed
apex needs it. With the step forcibly disabled, three of the four files **fail to decode at all**
(`prc_parse_tess_3d_compressed` returns a hard error), and the fourth decodes to a destroyed manifold
(3,529 boundary edges + 226 non-manifold edges of 7,167 total, Euler characteristic −1,591 where 2
is expected). This is not a subtle geometric approximation error — a decoder that omits this step
desynchronizes its own point-index bookkeeping and either aborts partway through decode or produces
grossly non-manifold output, on ordinary real files, not adversarial ones.

This is independently reproduced on a much larger, structurally unrelated 973-part, 397,645-triangle
real-world assembly: disabling the same step causes the entire file to fail to open
(`prc_api_open_contents` refuses to parse it), a stronger failure mode than any single curated file showed
individually.

### CR-18a — Insert the missing orientation step after Formula (3)

**Location:** §7.8.9.3 "Mesh Points and Triangles", immediately after Formula (3) and before the "In
Formula (1), V0 and V1 are taken so that..." sentence.

**BEFORE:**

> (3) `Y ← Z × X`
>
> In the Formula (1), V0 and V1 are taken so that V0 has a treatment index less than V1...

**AFTER:**

> (3) `Y ← Z × X`
>
> **(3a)** Let `w ← O - V3`. If `Y · w > 0`, negate both `Y` and `Z`. This orientation-consistency step
> is required: it ensures the reconstructed frame's `Y`/`Z` axes point away from the already-treated
> triangle `Tn`'s interior, consistently with the encoder's own choice when the same triangle was
> originally encoded. Applying Formulas (1)-(3) without this step reconstructs the correct frame only
> when `Y` happens to already satisfy this condition and
> produces a wrongly-oriented apex position for the rest, which desynchronizes point-index bookkeeping for
> every subsequently-decoded triangle that depends on it.
>
> In the Formula (1), V0 and V1 are taken so that V0 has a treatment index less than V1...

### CR-18b — Insert NOTE after the amended text

> **NOTE — This step is fatal to omit, not cosmetic.** A decoder that omits
> the step will either fail to decode or
> produces a non-manifold result. Implementations should treat it as a fundamental
> convention error, not a winding or rounding nuance.

**Confidence: High.** The missing step is already present, verified, and independently corroborated in
the companion *Pseudo-code Additions* document's `ApexFromEdge` function; this CR's contribution is
tracing that same requirement directly onto the base specification's own existing Formulas (1)-(3), which
have never themselves been corrected. Ablation-tested (not merely inferred) against five real files
spanning three orders of magnitude of mesh size.

---

## CR-18 Summary

| CR | Location | Change |
|---|---|---|
| CR-18a | §7.8.9.3 "Mesh Points and Triangles", after Formula (3) | Insert the missing orientation-consistency step (3a): negate `Y`/`Z` if `Y · (O - V3) > 0` |
| CR-18b | §7.8.9.3, after CR-18a | Insert NOTE: omitting this step is fatal (hard decode failure or gross manifold corruption), not a cosmetic winding issue |
title: PRC: Missing Orientation-Consistency in Apex Reconstruction

# PRC: mesh traversal has no termination condition, and no statement that an entity may hold multiple disjoint components

**Section:** §7.8.9.2 "Mesh Traversal" (`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc:2535`).

**Change type:** Normative addition.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(2 September 2026).

---

## The gap

§7.8.9.2 describes the stack discipline and then stops:

> To traverse the mesh structure.
>
> * If the current triangle has only one neighbour, this neighbour is pushed on the stack.
> * If the current triangle has both a left and a right neighbour which are not treated, the left
>   triangle is first pushed on the stack. Then the right triangle is pushed on the stack.
>
> Once done with the current triangle, the stack is popped and it becomes the current triangle.

That is the end of the subclause. **There is no termination condition.** The text does not say when
traversal finishes, and it never acknowledges that a single `PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` entity's
mesh may be more than one connected component.

The obvious reading — stop when the stack is empty — is wrong, and wrong silently. A mesh with
several disjoint components is encoded as several traversals back to back. A decoder that stops at
the first stack-drain produces the first component and discards the rest, with **no error and no
structural indication that anything is missing**.

## How often this matters

Sampling 60 compressed-tessellation entities from real files gathered from the wild, and deriving the
component count from `reference_array_size` (see
[#775](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/775) for the relation and its
corroboration):

| | |
|---|---|
| entities sampled | 60 |
| single component | 23 (38%) |
| **more than one component** | **37 (62%)** |
| most components in one entity | **7,211** |

So a decoder implementing the current text literally truncates the majority of real entities.

**The extreme case is worth seeing.** `GoldenCap_Example_Animated.stream-18` has
**C = 7,211 with T = 7,211** — every triangle is its own component, a fully disconnected mesh. A
first-drain decoder renders **one triangle out of 7,211**. `GranvilleIslandTotemPhotomodelerPDF3D.stream-100`
has 7,172 components across 1,126,444 triangles.

That entity also independently confirms the `#775` relation: if every triangle is isolated, each
contributes three reference entries, so `reference_array_size = 3T`; and `T + 2C` with `C = T` gives
exactly `3T`. The two arrive at the same number from different directions.

## CR-19a — proposed edit

Insert after "Once done with the current triangle, the stack is popped and it becomes the current
triangle.":

> A single `PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` entity's mesh is not required to form a single connected
> surface. It may consist of several disjoint components encoded back to back, each an independent
> seed triangle followed by its own traversal. The stack may therefore become empty more than once
> before the entity's triangles have all been produced; each such event after the first marks the
> boundary between one component's traversal and the next.
>
> A conforming decoder shall not terminate at the first stack-drain. It shall restart with a fresh
> seed triangle whenever the stack drains while triangles remain outstanding, and continue until the
> number of triangles produced equals the entity's triangle count.
>
> NOTE — A decoder that terminates at the first stack-drain silently omits every component after the
> first. There is no error condition and no structural indication that data is missing.

## Two corrections to our own original filing

**Terminology.** The original wrote "disjoint **shells**". That is wrong for this document:
`PRC_TYPE_TOPO_Shell` already exists (`07-base-entities.adoc:3096`) as a B-rep entity — "a collection
of faces which form either a closed or open boundary" — and belongs to exact geometry, not
tessellation traversal. Reusing the word invites confusion between two unrelated things. We have
switched to **component** and suggest the same substitution wherever the earlier wording was carried
into #775.

**A dangling reference.** The original text ended "until exactly `T` triangles have been produced,
where `T` is the entity's `triangle_face_array_size` (Table 175)". **There is no such field.**
Grepping the source, neither `triangle_face_array_size` nor `number_of_triangles` occurs anywhere;
the triangle count is never named, although three array lengths depend on it and a reader must
compute it to parse the entity at all. Our proposed text above therefore says "the entity's triangle
count" in words.

## One sentence unblocks three issues

The missing name for the triangle count is the common prerequisite for this issue,
[#772](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/772) (which needs it to state the
`normal_is_reversed` cardinality) and
[#775](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/775) (which needs it for
`reference_array_size = T + 2·C`). By parallel with the existing `face_number` definition at
`07-base-entities.adoc:2832`, one sentence in the same list would serve all three:

> `* The number of triangles is the number of elements in *triangle_face_array*.`

`triangle_face_array` is a `CompressedIndiceArray` and self-describing in length, so this names the
quantity without introducing a stored field.

**Suggested order:** the naming sentence, then this issue (which introduces the component concept),
then #775 (whose formula depends on both).

## Evidence class

The gap is readable from the text alone. The prevalence figures are ours, measured on a public
corpus; the derivation of component counts from `reference_array_size` is the relation under
discussion in #775, so for this issue it should be read as corroborating rather than independent. The
qualitative claim — that entities with multiple disjoint components exist and are common — does not
depend on that relation and can be confirmed by any decoder that counts stack-drain events.
title: PRC: `PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` Mesh Traversal Per-Component Restart on Multiple Disjoint Shells

# PRC: `reference_array_size` has no stated formula, only a tautological description

**Section:** §7.8.9.7 "Mesh Attribute Structure", Table 175 (Description of the Data Written to the
File), `reference_array_size` row.

**Change type:** Clarification — insert a NOTE giving the formula.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(2 September 2026), so the locations below can be acted on directly.

---

## The problem

In `iso-prc/definitions/base-entities/tessellation.yaml`, the Table 175 entry (line 539) reads:

```yaml
  - name: reference_array_size
    data_type:
      kind: UnsignedInteger
    required: true
    description: "*reference array size*"
```

The description restates the field name. Meanwhile the two arrays whose length it governs —
`points_is_reference_array` and `point_reference_array` — are both defined circularly against it
(`occurrence: reference_array_size`). So an encoder is told the size determines the arrays, and the
arrays determine nothing about the size. Nothing in the document says how to compute it.

**The same table one level up is better.** In Table 171 "Mesh Points and Triangles" (line 386) the
same field name carries:

```yaml
    description: "Size of *point_is_a_reference*"
```

which at least identifies what it sizes. The two tessellation tables are inconsistent with each
other on the same quantity.

## The formula

```
reference_array_size = T + 2·C
```

where `T` is the entity's triangle count and `C` is the number of disjoint connected components the
traversal decodes.

**Derivation, not curve-fit.** Each component contributes exactly 3 entries for its seed triangle's
three vertices, plus exactly 1 entry per subsequently-grown triangle's apex. For a component of `Tᵢ`
triangles that is `Tᵢ + 2` entries, and `Σ(Tᵢ + 2) = T + 2C` across all `C` components.

### Corroboration from real files

Sampling 60 compressed-tessellation entities from a corpus gathered from the wild, and taking
`reference_array_size − T`:

| | |
|---|---|
| entities sampled | 60 |
| difference always **even** | yes — 0 exceptions |
| difference always **positive** | yes — 0 exceptions |
| difference exactly `+2` (single component) | 23 of 60 (38%) |
| implied `C = difference / 2` | 1 to 7,211 |
| largest entity sampled | 1,126,444 triangles |

Under `T + 2·C` the difference is `2C`, so it must be even and at least 2. That is exactly what real
files show, without exception, across four orders of magnitude of entity size. A parity violation
anywhere in the sample would have falsified the formula; there were none.

## Two things that must be settled first

This CR cannot be written into the document as it stands, and both blockers are worth fixing on
their own account.

### 1. Neither `T` nor `C` has a name in the specification

Grepping the source: `triangle_face_array_size` and `number_of_triangles` do not occur anywhere. The
triangle count fixes the length of `edge_status_array`, `triangle_face_array` and
`normal_is_reversed`, and a reader must compute it to parse the entity — but the document never names
it. `face_number` **is** defined by contrast, at `07-base-entities.adoc:2832`.

This is raised in more detail on
[#772](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/772), where the same gap blocks stating
the `normal_is_reversed` cardinality. **One sentence fixes both**, suggested there as:

> `* The number of triangles is the number of elements in *triangle_face_array*.`

### 2. The multi-component concept does not exist in the traversal text

§7.8.9.2 "Mesh Traversal" (`07-base-entities.adoc:2535`) describes the stack discipline and ends:

> "Once done with the current triangle, the stack is popped and it becomes the current triangle."

There is **no termination condition**, and no statement that a fresh seed is chosen when the stack
drains with triangles still outstanding. So `C` refers to something the document does not currently
acknowledge exists. That is exactly what
[#774](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/774) asks for.

**So the natural order is #774, then the naming sentence, then this issue.** Applying this NOTE
first would reference two undefined quantities.

## A correction to our own earlier wording

Our original filing wrote this formula as `T + 2·S`, calling `S` the number of **shells**. That
terminology is wrong for this document: `shell` is already taken. `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_Shell`
(`07-base-entities.adoc:3096`) is a B-rep entity — "a collection of faces which form either a closed
or open boundary" — and belongs to exact geometry, not to tessellation traversal. Using the same word
for a disjoint tessellation component invites exactly the confusion the rest of this CR is trying to
remove.

We suggest **component** (or *connected component*) throughout, and have used it above. The same
substitution applies to #774.

## CR-20a — proposed edit

Once the two prerequisites are in, insert a NOTE after the `reference_array_size` row in Table 175:

> **NOTE** — `reference_array_size` shall equal `T + 2·C`, where `T` is the number of triangles and
> `C` is the number of disjoint components the traversal decodes (see the restart requirement in
> <<Mesh_Traversal>>). Each component contributes three entries for its seed triangle's vertices and
> one entry per subsequently-grown triangle's apex, giving `Tᵢ + 2` entries for a component of `Tᵢ`
> triangles. A conforming encoder shall set `reference_array_size` accordingly. A conforming decoder
> may use this relation to validate a parsed value against the entity's own triangle count and its
> own count of components encountered during traversal.

**Scope warning — do not apply this globally.** `reference_array_size` appears in **three** places in
`tessellation.yaml`:

| line | table | formula applies? |
|---|---|---|
| 386 | Mesh Points and Triangles | yes — same quantity |
| 539 | Description of the Data Written to the File | **yes — this is the target** |
| 696 | `CompressedTextureParameter` | **no** — different entity, unrelated meaning |

The texture-parameter field shares only the name. A blanket edit would attach a mesh-traversal
formula to a texture structure.
title: PRC: reference_array_size Has No Stated Formula, Only a Tautological Description

body:
# PRC: §10.2 gives no read-side procedure for Huffman-compressed arrays

**Section:** §10.2 "Huffman algorithm" (`iso-prc/sections/10-tessellation-compression.adoc:8`, with
its listing at `iso-prc/code/huffman.cpp`); §9.6 "WriteCharacterArray".

**Change type:** Normative addition.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(2 September 2026).

---

## The gap

§10.2 is entirely write-side. Its listing, `code/huffman.cpp`, is 88 lines and defines exactly two
functions — `AddBitInArray` and `Huffman` — both encoders. The subclause then ends:

> "Then the output unsigned integer array is used by `WriteCharacterArray` or `WriteShortArray` as
> described in <<IO_Algorithms>>."

There is **no counterpart for reading**. Grepping the source, no `UnHuffman`, no decode loop, and no
prose describing how a reader recovers the original array. A decoder implementer is given a complete
encoder and left to infer its inverse.

Two things in particular have to be inferred, and neither is guessable from the write side alone.

### 1. The container is not what it appears to be

`puHuffmanArray` is written with the same `WriteUnsignedInteger` calls used for ordinary integer
arrays, and Table 175 describes the result only as "an integer array obtained by the Huffman
algorithm". But the payload is the **individual bit values** of those words, not the words as 32-bit
units. The field carries a bit-packed sub-stream with its own cursor, independent of the file's
normal bitstream position.

A reader that treats this field the way it treats every other `Array<UnsignedInteger>` in the
specification — word-aligned — recovers nothing. Nothing in the current text warns of this.

### 2. The tree must be rebuilt before anything can be read

The decode is a bit-walk over a trie reconstructed from the stored leaf table. The storage format for
that table is described (that is what `huffman.cpp` shows), but the reconstruction and walk are not.

## Relationship to #770 — the two halves of the same gap

[#770](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/770) reports that
`HuffmanTreeCalculation` is declared and never defined — `code/huffman.cpp:3` ends in a semicolon,
and the function that builds the tree has no body anywhere in the document.

Taken together: **§10.2 currently specifies neither how to build the tree nor how to read it back.**
It specifies the middle — how a finished tree is serialised into a bit field. An encoder cannot
follow it without inventing the tree construction, and a decoder cannot follow it at all.

That framing may be more useful to the committee than either issue alone. If only one is taken, the
read side is the more damaging omission, because an encoder at least has working output to compare
against, whereas a decoder has nothing.

## CR-21a — insert a read-side procedure

Add to §10.2, after the `Huffman()` listing, a procedure that:

1. reads the leaf table as stored by the existing listing — leaf count, maximum code length, and per
   leaf its value, code length and code;
2. reconstructs the trie from those codes, most significant bit first, the highest bit of a code
   corresponding to the root (this is already stated for the encoder in the NOTE under
   <<tab-encoding>> and should be restated on the read side);
3. walks the trie bit by bit over the payload, emitting a value on reaching each leaf, until
   `uCharArraySize` values have been produced.

The termination condition matters and should be explicit: decoding is driven by the **expected
element count**, not by exhausting the payload. The final word is padded and its trailing bits are
not a code.

## CR-21b — insert a NOTE on the container

At §9.6 "WriteCharacterArray" where it invokes `Huffman()`, and/or in §10.2 before the listing:

> **NOTE** — Although the Huffman output is written using the same integer-array calls used elsewhere
> in this document, its payload is the sequence of *bit values* of those words rather than the words
> themselves, and is read with a bit cursor independent of the enclosing bitstream. A reader that
> consumes this field as an ordinary word-aligned `Array<UnsignedInteger>` will not recover the
> original data.

## Evidence

The absence is readable from the source: two encoder functions, no decoder, no read prose.

That the inferred read procedure is correct is confirmed by implementation. Our decoder implements it
as described above and parses a 310-file corpus of real files gathered from the wild; every
Huffman-coded field in every file that decodes at all passes through this path.

**There is now a second, independent confirmation.** A separate implementation, working from its own
corpus of 529 PRC files, reconstructed the exponent Huffman table and verified it against the
specification's own listing entry by entry — 2,077 of 2,077 — while investigating
[#769](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/769). That is two readers, built
separately, arriving at the same reconstruction of a procedure the document does not contain.

We can supply the procedure in the document's pseudocode style if that would help.
title: PRC: No Read-Side Procedure Given for Huffman-Compressed Arrays

body: **Hello PDF Association community,** I am writing to seek clarification regarding the specifications of the `RD` entries within FreeText annotations. When referencing **ISO 32000-2:2020 (PDF 2.0) Second edition: 2020-12** alongside **Errata Collection 3 (June 1, 2026)**, there appears to be a discrepancy between the specification text and how Adobe Acrobat currently processes this entry. In *ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf*, under **Table 177 — Additional entries specific to a free text annotation**, the description for the `RD` entry explicitly states: > *"The order of elements in the array can be interpreted as [left, top, right, bottom]."* However, based on our testing, Adobe Acrobat seems to generate and process this array in the order of **[left, bottom, right, top]**. For example, when creating a FreeTextCallout in Acrobat, the resulting `RD` array is written as `[20 0.5 0.5 40]`, which visually and structurally aligns with the `[left, bottom, right, top]` ordering. (I have attached a sample file, **"Acrobat_RD.pdf"**, which demonstrates this behavior). Could the community or specification authors please clarify: 1. Is the `[left, top, right, bottom]` order in the current specification and EC3 definitively correct, meaning Acrobat's implementation is non-standard? 2. Or, is this a known typographical error in the specification that might need to be addressed in a future errata? Thank you in advance for your time and guidance! **Attachments:** [Acrobat_RD.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334669/Acrobat_RD.pdf)

**Describe the bug**
This might not be a bug itself, but I found that in 9.10.3 Example 2, the tounicode cmap has name `Adobe-Identity-UCS2`, this is different from ISO 32000-1:2008 `Adobe-Identity-UCS`. I wonder if this change is intentional, and which is the recommended name nowadays.

* 9.10.3 Example 2 shows that ROS can be set to `Adobe-UCS2-0`, but ISO 32000-1 it is `Adobe-UCS-0`. Which is more correct for a latin-based `ToUnicode` CMap?

*  9.10.3 Example 2 shows that `CMapType` can be set to 2. And only in `5411.ToUnicode.pdf` mentions that
```text
Note from the above excerpt that /CMapType is set to 2 in “ToUnicode” mapping files.
```
It seems this is mentioned nowhere within 32000.

* `5014.CIDFont_Spec.pdf` pg 35 says "A CMap file must begin with the comment characters `%!`; otherwise it may
not be given the appropriate handling in some operating system environments.
The first line in the file is `%!PS-Adobe-3.0 Resource-CMap`". This line is not observed within the 9.10.3 Example 2 example. Is it optional, or forbidden within CMap streams?

* `5411.ToUnicode.pdf` pg 3 says
```text
Because a “ToUnicode” mapping file is used to convert from CIDs (which begin at decimal 0,
which is expressed as 0x0000 in hexadecimal notation) to Unicode code points, the following
“codespacerange” definition, without exception, shall always be used:
1 begincodespacerange
<0000> <FFFF>
endcodespacerange
```
we all know that in PDF spec it specially calls out that 
```text
The CMap file shall contain begincodespacerange and endcodespacerange operators 
that are consistent with the encoding that the font uses. In particular, for a simple font,
the codespace shall be one byte long.
```
so they're somewhat different.

According to 7.5.8.2 of ISO 32000-2:2020, cross-reference streams (and strings in their stream dictionaries) are not encrypted.

According to 7.6.2, cross-reference streams (and strings in their stream dictionaries) are encrypted as they do not appear in the list of objects not to be encrypted.

I think 7.5.8.2 is correct and 7.6.2 is wrong as encryption dictionaries need not be direct objects. There would be a chicken-and-egg problem with an indirect encryption dictionary and an encrypted cross-reference stream pointing to it.

Therefore, I suggest adding cross-reference streams (and strings in their stream dictionaries) to the list of objects not to be encrypted in 7.6.2.
title: Encryption of cross-reference streams

body:
The remainder modulo 3 of a base-256 number can be computed (like the remainder modulo 3 of a decimal number) as the remainder modulo 3 of the digit sum (due to 256%3==1 and 10%3==1). That is, instead of

> Taking the first 16 bytes of E as an unsigned big-endian integer, compute the remainder, modulo 3.

we can just

> Compute the sum of the first 16 bytes of E and compute the remainder of the sum, modulo  3.

avoiding use of a BigInteger. It follows that the result will be the same no matter whether interpreting the first 16 bytes of E as big-endian integer or as little-endian integer. Same digit sum.

Perhaps worth a note, but not more.
title: The description of step c in Algorithm 2.B in 7.6.4.3.4 of ISO 32000-2:2020 is overly complicated

# PRC: §4.2 mandates version 10001, which deployed readers refuse

**Clause:** §4.2 "Versioning" (`iso-prc/sections/04-file-concepts.adoc:127-142`).

**Category:** Technical, internal consistency, with a measured interoperability consequence.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `567be68` (20 November 2026). The clause has not
changed since `ba2bdc1`, the commit this issue was first written against, so the line numbers are the same.

**Revised 21 November 2026.** The first version of this description proposed a replacement for line 134 only. Datalogics' comment of
24 September (Patrick Gallot) and a later review of his (14 November 2026) showed that the replacement left two other sentences of the clause saying the opposite, and gave a
version that holds together. This description is revised to that version; the problem and the evidence are unchanged apart from the
added figures.

---

## Summary

§4.2 uses one number for two different jobs: the identifier of *this document's edition*, and the value a conforming file must carry
in `minimal_version_for_read`. They are not the same thing, and conflating them makes the clause self-defeating: a file that satisfies
line 134 must be refused, under line 138, by every reader in the field.

**The requested change keeps 10001 as the edition version.** The edition is recorded in `authoring_version`, which is what line 138
already says it is. What a reader needs, `minimal_version_for_read`, is set by the file's content, and for content defined wholly by
this document that is 8137, the highest version at which this document defines any content.

## The clause as it stands

Line 132:

> Version numbers consist of the year modulo 2000 followed by three digits representing the day of the year. This document shall have
> the version 10001, corresponding to the first day of the year 2010.

Line 134:

> This international standard specifies the PRC version10001. Documents with other PRC versions are non-compliant as they may alter the
> behaviour and presentation of content.

Line 138 (the sentences on the two fields):

> The *authoring_version* represents the version of this document that the PRC file writer conformed to at the time the FileHeader or the
> FileStructure was written. The *minimal_version_for_read* represents the version of the international standard that a PRC file reader
> shall conform to successfully read the FileHeader or the FileStructure. If the *current_version* of the PRC file reader is less than the
> *minimal_version_for_read*, then the PRC file reader shall not continue to process the file and report an error.

Line 140:

> If *minimal_version_for_read* is lower than *authoring_version*, the PRC file writer shall write a schema description in the PRC file
> providing the differences between the two versions of this document. The schema description enables a PRC file reader to read and skip
> new information since these new data cannot be interpreted as they are from a newer version.

## The problem

Line 134 requires files to be version 10001. Line 138 requires a reader whose `current_version` is below a file's
`minimal_version_for_read` to refuse it. **The dominant deployed reader's `current_version` is 8137.** So a file complying with line 134
is refused, correctly, under line 138. Line 132 is not the problem: a document may identify its own edition by publication date. The
problem is that line 134 turns that identifier into a requirement on file content.

**10001 gates nothing.** A survey of the complete draft finds only four version-valued references: **8030** (an optional
directional-light field), **8137** (the version defining the general transformation entity, §8.4.2), **9149** (illustrative, inside a
worked schema example, §8.4.4) and **10001** itself. **The highest version at which this document defines any content is 8137.** The
8137 to 10001 delta is empty, so line 134 mandates a value that expresses nothing the earlier value cannot express, and costs
interoperability with the installed base.

### Why a replacement of line 134 alone does not work

Three sentences of §4.2 have to agree, and the first replacement proposed here did not make them agree (Datalogics, 14 November 2026):

1. **The first sentence gave two answers.** "A conforming writer shall set `minimal_version_for_read` to the lowest version at which all
   of the file's content is defined; for content defined wholly by this document that value is 8137." All content in a conforming file is
   defined by this document, so the second half fixes the value at 8137 for every such file. The first half does not: this document gates
   content at two versions only, 8030 for the optional directional-light field and 8137 for `PRC_TYPE_MISC_GeneralTransformation`. A file
   that uses neither has its lowest defined version below 8137. That is not a corner case: in the 529 files of Datalogics' comment, 178
   declare 7094 or 7095 (153 and 25), and all 73 that were authored above 8137 declare one of those two. Under the first half those files may be
   conforming; under the second they are not.
2. **Line 138 writes 10001 into every file anyway.** It defines `authoring_version` as "the version of this document that the PRC file
   writer conformed to". The version of this document is 10001, so a writer working to this edition records 10001 there, and the
   replacement's sentence that 10001 "is not itself written into a file" is untrue of the very next field. The same sentence defines
   `minimal_version_for_read` as "the version of the international standard that a PRC file reader shall conform to", which is an
   edition number again. §4.2 treats both fields as edition numbers throughout.
3. **Line 140 would turn every conforming file into a schema obligation.** If `minimal_version_for_read` is lower than
   `authoring_version`, the writer shall write a schema describing the differences. With line 138 a writer following the replacement
   writes 8137 below 10001 and so owes a schema describing a difference that, by this issue's own survey, is empty. Writing the two
   fields equal is what exempts the nanoPRC writer today.

There is also a smaller point in the NOTE: "A writer that requires content defined after 8137 uses the `authoring_version` and schema
mechanism ..., rather than raising `minimal_version_for_read`" says what a writer is to do, and the ISO Directives do not allow a note to
carry a requirement, recommendation, permission or instruction (Part 2, 24.5). It can stay as a note if turned into a statement of fact,
or become body text with "shall".

## Evidence

**Reader ceiling, measured by bisection.** Holding a known-good file constant and varying only the declared `minimal_version_for_read`:
**8137 accepted, 8138 refused.** A one-unit boundary, on a fully updated 2026 Adobe Acrobat installation; Datalogics found the same boundary
independently on Acrobat DC 26.2.21931.0 (comment of 24 September). Refusal presents as a version
dialog, distinct from any content-level failure. Holding `authoring_version` at 23306 and varying `minimal_version_for_read` gives the
same boundary, so `authoring_version` gates nothing in Acrobat; before that, files written with 7094 and 23306 opened.

**Installed base (nanoPRC, header fields of the public prc-db collection, 606 files; the header could be read in 603).**

| declared | files |
|---|--:|
| `minimal_version_for_read` and `authoring_version` both 8137 | 228 |
| `minimal_version_for_read` below 8137 (7094 or 7095) | 375 |
| `minimal_version_for_read` above 8137 | 0 |
| `authoring_version` above `minimal_version_for_read` | 365 |

(Counted from the header fields only; whether each file also carries a schema was not counted here, see the Datalogics figures below.)
Independently developed writers converge on 8137.

**Datalogics' 529 files (comment of 24 September).** Public prc-db plus a SafeDocs-derived set, fields read from the uncompressed header: floor 8137 in 351
files, 7094 in 153, 7095 in 25, **none above 8137**; 73 files were authored above 8137 (up to 20225) and every one of them declares a floor of 7094 or 7095
(61 and 12). Writers newer than the mandate still encode a floor well below it: in practice `minimal_version_for_read` means the oldest reader that
can cope with the content, not the edition the file was written against. The same comment notes that a writer which decouples the two fields would
owe a schema under line 140 as it stands, which is the third problem above.

**Content that bears on the floor (Datalogics, 14 November 2026).** The only content this document gates by version that bears on the
floor is `PRC_TYPE_MISC_GeneralTransformation` (8137); the 8030 `intensity` field is gated on `authoring_version`, not on the floor, so it
does not enter. Among files declaring a floor below 8137 (377 in prc-db at 606 files, 81 in Datalogics' SafeDocs set of 219), 96 and 47
carry general transformations (51,211 and 15,113 of them), and every one of those files has a schema declaring the type: 96 of 96 and 47
of 47. The files declaring 8137 carry it without a schema in 116 and 5 of them, as they are entitled to. Under the rule below, nothing in
either collection changes its standing.

**The escape hatch already works.** Files that declare an `authoring_version` above their `minimal_version_for_read` (up to 2023) carry a
schema describing the difference and open correctly in the 2008-era reader. The migration mechanism §4.2 provides is in active, successful
field use, and this issue asks for nothing that changes it.

## Proposed change

**Keep line 132's identification of the edition, in the form of a fact:** "The version of this document is 10001, corresponding to the
first day of the year 2010." (Line 132's "This document shall have the version 10001" puts a requirement on a document, not on a reader or
a writer.)

**Replace line 134** with:

> This document defines content up to version 8137. A PRC file writer shall set *minimal_version_for_read* of a FileHeader or a
> FileStructure to a value that is at least the highest version at which any content it contains is defined, other than content described
> by a schema in the file (see below), and shall not exceed 8137 when all of that content is defined by this document.

**In line 138**, keep the account of `authoring_version` (a file written to this edition records 10001), and replace the sentence on
`minimal_version_for_read` ("the version of the international standard that a PRC file reader shall conform to successfully read the
FileHeader or the FileStructure") with one that agrees with the rule above: the lowest version a PRC file reader needs to read it. Line 130
reads the same way and changes with it, so that §4.2 gives one account.

**At the end of line 140** add:

> No schema description is required when the file contains no content defined between the two versions.

so that a file at 10001 with a floor of 8137 needs no schema when it holds nothing newer than its floor. The test is on the file, not on
the document: a file at 8137 and 10001 needs no schema; a file at 7094 that carries general transformations needs one and already has one;
a file at 7094 that carries nothing newer needs none.

**Turn the NOTE into a statement of fact or into body text** (see above): for example, "Content defined after 8137 is read through the
schema mechanism described below, not through a higher `minimal_version_for_read`."

**Editorial, in the same lines:** "This international standard" should be "This document" (Part 2, 10.6); "A conforming writer" should be
"A PRC file writer", the defined term (3.1); the field names go in bold as elsewhere in the clause. "PRC version10001", the missing space,
goes with line 134.

### Two decisions for the group

- **A range, not a fixed value.** The rule states a floor ("no lower than the content needs") and a ceiling ("no higher than this
  document defines"). It keeps the intent, settles point 1 without choosing between the 7094 and 8137 files (both are conforming if their
  content allows), and leaves the reader rule in line 138 alone. The exception for schema-described content is what keeps line 140
  working: that mechanism exists so that a file can carry content newer than its floor.
- **`authoring_version` holds 10001 for a file written to this edition.** `minimal_version_for_read` records what a reader needs; the two
  jobs are then separate fields. Nothing is lost in the field: `authoring_version` gates nothing, so a deployed reader at 8137 still opens
  a new file whose `minimal_version_for_read` is 8137 or lower, and files already written at 7094, 7095 or 8137 are unaffected.
  **The alternative** is for `authoring_version` to hold 8137, with line 138 rewritten to mean the highest version of content the writer
  conforms to, which leaves line 140 needing no exception. We prefer 10001 because it keeps the edition identifiable in every new file,
  where the alternative leaves no record of it in the file at all. It is a change for writers that put 8137 in both fields today.

### What this does and does not reach

With line 138's account of `authoring_version` standing as written, what changes with line 134 is line 138's sentence on
`minimal_version_for_read`, line 130, and the sentence that 10001 "is not itself written into a file", which goes. So the change is larger
than "line 134 only". It also reaches the document title ("PRC 10001", `document.adoc:7` and `:10`) and the scope ("requirements for
the PRC 10001", `01-scope.adoc:4`); both are right as names of the edition and need no change.

The worked example at §8.4.4 (`08-schema-defs.adoc:532`), whose versioned block is gated on 9149, is a separate matter: it concerns the
version a reader claims, not the one a writer writes, and no wording of line 134 changes it.

## Scope

This request concerns the version values and the sentences that define them. It does not propose changing the version encoding, the
`minimal_version_for_read` / `authoring_version` mechanism or the schema-delta requirement, all of which are demonstrably sound and in
active field use.

---

*Version numbers decode as (year mod 2000) x 1000 + day of year, per §4.2. Reader measurements taken August 2026 against a fully updated
Adobe Acrobat installation. Header counts for prc-db: nanoPRC, November 2026. The analysis of lines 138 and 140, the range wording and the
count of files with floors below 8137 are by Datalogics (Patrick Gallot, 14 November 2026).*
title: PRC: §4.2 mandates version 10001, which deployed readers refuse

# PRC: `PRC_HCG_Ellipse` is emitted by §9.17 but has no structure, and cannot be skipped

**Sections:** §7.9.21.9.1 "General" (`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc:3926–3928`);
§9.17 "WriteCompressedEntityType" (`iso-prc/code/WriteCompressedEntityType.cpp`); Table 204
"Enumeration of Compressed Entity Types" (`iso-prc/definitions/values/value_type.yaml:121–123`).

**Change type:** Normative correction. The document defines how to *emit* a curve type for which it
defines no content, and simultaneously declares that type unused.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(4 September 2026). No commit in that repository references this issue.

---

## The contradiction

§7.9.21.9.1 enumerates the permitted compressed curve types and excludes ellipse
(`07-base-entities.adoc:3926`, then `:3928`):

> A compressed curve is one of _PRC_HCG_Line_, _PRC_HCG_Circle_, _PRC_HCG_BsplineHermiteCurve_ or
> _PRC_HCG_CompositeCurve_.
>
> The curve type PRC_HCG_Ellipse is reserved for future use.

Notwithstanding that reservation, the normative writer example for exactly this field contains a live
case that emits it (`WriteCompressedEntityType.cpp:20–22`):

```c
case PRC_HCG_Ellipse :
// writing 2 bits (11) then 2 other (00)
return WriteUnsignedIntegerWithVariableBitNumber ((3 << 2) + 0 , 4);
```

So the curve-type field is a prefix code in which `11` is an escape introducing two further bits:

| type | bits | value |
|---|---|---|
| `PRC_HCG_Line` | `00` | 0 |
| `PRC_HCG_Circle` | `01` | 1 |
| `PRC_HCG_BsplineHermiteCurve` | `10` | 2 |
| `PRC_HCG_Ellipse` | `11` `00` | 12 |
| `PRC_HCG_CompositeCurve` | `11` `01` | 13 |

That also explains the otherwise puzzling numbering in Table 204 "Enumeration of Compressed Entity
Types", where the compressed *curve* types run 0, 1, 2 and then jump to 12 and 13: those values are the four-bit codes themselves, not arbitrary
identifiers.

## Why this is a decode hazard, not an unused reservation

**No structure is defined for the type anywhere in the document.** The compressed curve structures
present in the source are `PRC_HCG_Line`, `PRC_HCG_Circle` (with `ParticularCircle` and
`GeneralCircle`), `PRC_HCG_BsplineHermiteCurve` and `PRC_HCG_CompositeCurve`. Enumerating every
`PRC_HCG_*` structure table in the working source returns seventeen entities, and **none of them is
an ellipse**. No prose states what bits follow the code `1100`.

Because the document assigns the type a concrete four-bit code but no length and no content, a
conforming reader that encounters `1100`:

- cannot decode the entity, because nothing defines its fields; and
- **cannot skip it either**, because nothing defines its length.

The bitstream is unrecoverable from that point. A reserved type that is never emitted is harmless; a
reserved type with a normative encoding and no structure is a hazard, because a writer following
§9.17 literally is entitled to emit it.

## Corpus evidence, supporting Option A

We swept a 310-file corpus gathered from the wild for the compressed curve type codes. Only **20 of
those files carry any compressed curve at all** — most contain no compressed B-rep — but between them
those 20 hold **152,345 compressed curves**:

| type | code | count | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRC_HCG_Line` | `00` | 78,455 | 51.5% |
| `PRC_HCG_Circle` | `01` | 62,584 | 41.1% |
| `PRC_HCG_BsplineHermiteCurve` | `10` | 11,306 | 7.4% |
| `PRC_HCG_CompositeCurve` | `1101` | **0** | — |
| `PRC_HCG_Ellipse` | `1100` | **0** | — |

Across 152,345 real compressed curves the escape prefix `11` is never used at all — neither four-bit
code occurs.

We state the denominator deliberately: "none in 310 files" would overstate this, since only 20 could
ever have contained one. What the measurement supports is the narrower claim that in 152,345 observed
compressed curves there is no instance of either four-bit type. That is not proof none exists
elsewhere, and the committee is better placed to establish whether any writer emits the code. The
asymmetry is worth stating plainly: a wrongly-adopted Option A renders real files unreadable, whereas
a wrongly-adopted Option B merely documents a type nobody emits.

**A caution against a tempting false lead.** The *uncompressed* ellipse, Table 262
`PRC_TYPE_CRV_Ellipse`, is fully specified — including a radius per axis, evaluated as
`X = rx·cos(t)`, `Y = ry·sin(t)`. Its existence, and SDK support for it, says nothing about the
compressed type: PRC defines the compressed curve forms separately and they are not the uncompressed
structures reused, as the `ParticularCircle` / `GeneralCircle` split shows. We mention it because we
briefly mistook one for the other ourselves.

## CR-23a — resolve the contradiction, in one of two directions

The committee's choice; the defect is that the document currently asserts both.

**Option A — treat §9.17 as the error (RECOMMENDED, on the evidence above).** Delete the
`case PRC_HCG_Ellipse` branch from `WriteCompressedEntityType.cpp`, and add to §7.9.21.9.1 after the
existing reservation sentence:

> The value `1100` is reserved and shall not be written. A reader encountering it shall treat the
> compressed B-rep data as malformed, since the length of the reserved entity is undefined and the
> bitstream cannot be resynchronized.

**Option B — treat §7.9.21.9.1 as the error.** If an ellipse encoding is in fact intended, add the
corresponding structure table alongside the existing compressed curve tables, amend §7.9.21.9.1's
enumeration to include `PRC_HCG_Ellipse`, and delete the "reserved for future use" sentence.

We do not propose a field list. We have never seen such a file, and a structure table guessed from the
uncompressed ellipse's parameters would be exactly the kind of invention this issue objects to §9.17
inviting. If the committee takes this direction, the layout should come from an implementation that
actually emits the code.

**What would settle the choice quickly:** a single file containing a `PRC_HCG_Ellipse`. Its existence
decides for B and confirms the field order directly; continued absence across the committee's own
corpora decides for A.

## CR-23b — NOTE on the escape prefix

Whichever option is taken, the prefix structure is worth stating in the base text rather than leaving
it to be inferred from the §9.17 sample, which is the only place the two-then-two-bit escape is
visible:

> **NOTE** — The compressed curve type is a variable-length prefix code. Values `00`, `01` and `10`
> are complete in two bits. The prefix `11` introduces two further bits, giving the four-bit values
> `1100` and `1101`. A reader must therefore read two bits, and only read two more if the first two
> are both set.

## CR-23c — two editorial defects in the same listing

Both are in `WriteCompressedEntityType.cpp` and were found only by reading the working source; they
are not visible in the published PDF.

1. **Stray character terminating the listing.** Line 26 ends with a `0` after the semicolon:
   `return WriteUnsignedIntegerWithVariableBitNumber ((3 << 2) + 1 , 4);0` — the trailing `0` is not
   valid C and should be deleted.
2. **Identifier spelled inconsistently.** Line 16 uses `PRC_HCG_BSplineHermiteCurve` (capital S). Every
   other occurrence in the document — seven of them, across `07-base-entities.adoc`, `topology.yaml`
   and `value_type.yaml` — uses `PRC_HCG_BsplineHermiteCurve`. The listing should match.

## Relationship to #727 and the #769–#776 series

This finding comes from the same specification review as
[#727](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/727), and is filed separately for the
same reason that review's earlier findings became
[#769](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/769)–[#776](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/776):
each is independently actionable and independently closable, and bundling them delays the
straightforward ones behind the contested ones.

It is **not** a continuation of #727's open question. #727 concerns `is_face_planar` interpretation
within `PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` — tessellation — and remains open pending a discriminating
fixture. This issue concerns the compressed B-rep exact-geometry text and does not depend on how
#727 resolves. The two share a provenance, not a subject.

## Scope

This issue is §7.9.21.9.1 and §9.17 only. The two neighbouring findings in the same stretch of text are
filed as their own issues in this series: the dangling `number_of_bits_to_store_reference` cross-reference in §7.9.21.8, and
the unstated orientation of implicit iso-face curves in §7.9.21.5.1.

**Provenance.** Surfaced while working through the compressed-B-rep curve material alongside the
nanoPRC maintainer (CascadiaVoxel LLC, AGPLv3, https://github.com/mvrhel/nanoPRC), who is
implementing the compressed exact-geometry path and hit this against a real file. Verifiable by
reading the specification alone; no implementation dependency.

# PRC: dangling `number_of_bits_to_store_reference` cross-reference in §7.9.21.8

**Sections:** §7.9.21.8 "RefOrCompressedCurve" (`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc:3912`);
§7.9.20 "PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress" (`iso-prc/sections/07-base-entities.adoc:3232`).

**Change type:** Editorial correction.

**Verified against:** the working source at `pdf-association/3dpdf-twg`, `main` @ `ba2bdc1`
(4 September 2026). No commit in that repository references this issue.

---

## Finding

§7.9.21.8 states (`07-base-entities.adoc:3912`):

> The index is stored with a variable number of bits indicated by *number_of_bits_to_store_reference*.
> See <<PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress>> for a definition of this number when decoding within
> _PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress_, and <<PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress>> when decoding within
> PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress."

The first half is correct: `number_of_bits_to_store_reference` is defined under
`PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress` (`07-base-entities.adoc:3251`).

**The second half points at nothing.** `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress` lists exactly four
members — the type tag, `base` (`ContentBody`), `curve_tolerance` (`Double`) and `compressed_curve`
(`CompressedCurve`) — and contains no such field. The same subclause states the opposite of the
cross-reference's premise (`07-base-entities.adoc:3232`):

> NOTE: Unlike _PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress_, the _PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress_ structure
> contains no downstream topological network arrays. Consequently, the variables
> number_vertex_references and number_edge_references specified in _PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress_
> are omitted entirely from this bitstream scope as they are architecturally non-applicable.

**There is no interoperability consequence.** A single wire body holds one `CompressedCurve`, never a
`RefOrCompressedCurve`, so no index is read and the bit count is never needed. The cost is purely
implementor time — the cross-reference invites a search for a definition that does not exist, in a
subclause that explicitly says it should not.

## CR-24a — correct the cross-reference

**BEFORE:**

> See 7.9.21 for a definition of this number when decoding within `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress`,
> and 7.9.20 when decoding within `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress`.

**AFTER:**

> See 7.9.21 for a definition of this number. It applies only when decoding within
> `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_BrepDataCompress`; `RefOrCompressedCurve` does not occur within
> `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress`, which contains a single `CompressedCurve` and no reference
> indices (see the NOTE in 7.9.20).

## CR-24b — two markup defects in the same sentence

Visible only in the working source, and cheap to fix while the sentence is being edited:

1. **Unmatched quotation mark.** Line 3912 ends `...within PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress."` —
   a closing double quote with no opening one anywhere in the sentence.
2. **Missing italic markup.** That final `PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress` is plain text, while
   every other entity name in the same sentence is marked up as `_..._`. It should be
   `_PRC_TYPE_TOPO_SingleWireBodyCompress_`.

## Relationship to #727 and the #769–#776 series

This finding comes from the same specification review as
[#727](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/727), and is filed separately for the
same reason that review's earlier findings became
[#769](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/769)–[#776](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/issues/776):
each is independently actionable and independently closable, and bundling them delays the
straightforward ones behind the contested ones.

It is **not** a continuation of #727's open question. #727 concerns `is_face_planar` interpretation
within `PRC_TYPE_TESS_3D_Compressed` — tessellation — and remains open pending a discriminating
fixture. This issue concerns the compressed B-rep exact-geometry text and does not depend on how
#727 resolves. The two share a provenance, not a subject.

## Scope

This issue is the §7.9.21.8 cross-reference only. The two neighbouring findings in the same stretch of
text are filed as their own issues in this series: `PRC_HCG_Ellipse` having a normative encoding but no structure, and the
unstated orientation of implicit iso-face curves in §7.9.21.5.1.

**Provenance.** Surfaced while working through the compressed-B-rep curve material alongside the
nanoPRC maintainer (CascadiaVoxel LLC, AGPLv3, https://github.com/mvrhel/nanoPRC), who is
implementing the compressed exact-geometry path and hit this against a real file. Verifiable by
reading the specification alone; no implementation dependency.
